trust_decision.summary: Java deserialisation (readObject / serialization proxy) trusts a stream-supplied element count as a presizing hint and allocates backing arrays of that size; the fix caps the hint at 256 in CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet and MapMakerInternalMap (jre + android flavours).

landing_point.why: "Eager array allocation during deserialization" leads straight to readObject methods that call init(readInt()); CompactHashMap is the most obvious one, and its init feeds allocArrays (CompactHashMap.java:265-275).

fix_sites.entry_point: ObjectInputStream.readObject on a stream naming CompactHashMap/CompactLinkedHashMap (e.g. backing map of a Multimaps.newMultimap custom multimap, Multimaps.java:305)
ObjectInputStream.readObject on a stream naming CompactHashSet/CompactLinkedHashSet
ObjectInputStream.readObject of a map from MapMaker().weakKeys()/weakValues().makeMap() via SerializationProxy.readObject (MapMakerInternalMap.java:2894-2898)
fix_sites.module_kind: serialization proxy -> builder (MapMaker) in concurrent map internals (jre flavour)

fix_sites.entry_point: ObjectInputStream.readObject; android flavour also uses CompactHashMap as default backing map (android/guava/src/com/google/common/collect/Platform.java:36, MultimapBuilder.java:88)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: guava/src/com/google/common/collect/MapMakerInternalMap.java:2848-2856 (size read in serialization proxy, passed through MapMaker.initialCapacity builder; allocation happens in MapMakerInternalMap constructor :173-199)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: MapMakerInternalMap is an internal concurrent map whose proxy only feeds a builder 'hint' and whose constructor already clamps to MAXIMUM_CAPACITY (MapMakerInternalMap.java:173); a solver focused on Compact* init() can argue it is a different class and already bounded. Project comments also say no program should deserialise hostile input (guava/src/com/google/common/collect/EnumHashBiMap.java:129-133).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: init(expectedSize) is shared with the public presizing API createWithExpectedSize; capping inside init()/allocArrays instead of at the readObject call breaks presizing (tests assert backing arrays have exactly expectedSize length).

O6_input_shapes: element count read by readInt() in custom readObject (CompactHashMap/CompactHashSet, inherited by CompactLinkedHashMap/CompactLinkedHashSet)
size read by readInt() in a serialization proxy and routed through a builder's initialCapacity (MapMakerInternalMap)

O7_producer.where: guava/src/com/google/common/collect/CompactHashMap.java:265-275 (allocArrays, lazy allocation at first put during readObject loop); guava/src/com/google/common/collect/MapMakerInternalMap.java:186-199 (segment/table allocation in constructor)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MapMakerInternalMap serialization proxy: stream-supplied concurrencyLevel field (defaultReadObject) still drives segment count up to MAX_SEGMENTS=65536 after the fix; bounded, much smaller amplification than the size hint.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Already clamped to 1<<16 by the constructor; not the 'size' the advisory talks about.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as a fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: LocalCache Manual/LoadingSerializationProxy: stream-supplied concurrencyLevel rebuilds a cache with up to 65536 eagerly allocated segments; initialCapacity is not serialised, so no size hint.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different package (cache), already clamped at MAX_SEGMENTS, and not a stream size hint.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class constructor already does exactly that (HashMultiset.java:75); a maintainer could reuse it in readObject for efficiency.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: newBackingMap(distinctElements) instead of DEFAULT_SIZE (ObjectCountHashMap eager arrays)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Presizing from the read count is a natural micro-optimisation in the android multiset path, far from Compact*.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: allocate long[length] directly from readInt() instead of the growing builder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Arrays of known length are usually allocated directly; distant package (util.concurrent).
distinctKeys is read immediately above; the constant 12 looks arbitrary.

O10_build.project_tests: guava-tests/test/com/google/common/collect/CompactHashMapTest.java, CompactHashSetTest.java, MapMakerInternalMapTest.java (+ android/guava-tests copies); collection testlib suites incl. serialization

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Clamp the count inside CompactHashMap.init()/allocArrays (breaking createWithExpectedSize presizing) or only fix CompactHashMap and miss CompactHashSet, MapMakerInternalMap and the android copies.

out_of_scope_notes: BloomFilter.readFrom(in, funnel) defaults maxAllowedSizeInBits to Long.MAX_VALUE (guava/src/com/google/common/hash/BloomFilter.java:650-652); this is a separate custom binary format with an opt-in cap, not Java serialisation.
CacheBuilderSpec parses initialCapacity from a developer config string (guava/src/com/google/common/cache/CacheBuilderSpec.java:180); that is config, not deserialisation.
